How this was built data engine · fix-up rules · checks

Data engine

Each game's box score and play-by-play come from the CollegeBasketballData.com API and are saved in a local database. Who was on the floor, second by second, is rebuilt from the substitutions in the play-by-play. Box score minutes are the official record.

This copy is a sample: last season's (2025–26) games, with 8 games from Jan 24 2026 picked as the slate.

Fix-up rules

The substitution feed has glitches. When a new kind can be fixed safely, the fix becomes a written rule, applied before the checks run. There are two so far.

Example, found while testing this season's first games: in UT Martin @ Tulane (Nov 2 2026, double overtime), Tulane subbed a player out and reversed the swap at the same timestamp. The feed paired the two substitutions wrongly and left 6 players on the floor for 6 seconds. The rule: cancel any swap reversed at the same timestamp, then check the game again. A game that still fails is marked “data issue” and stays in the report.

Checks

  • Every game is checked: exactly 5 players per team on the floor at every moment, team minutes add up to 200 (plus 25 per overtime), and every player within 1 minute of the box score. A game that fails is marked “data issue” and stays in: its box score minutes still count, while numbers built from play-by-play leave it out. The footer counts these games.
  • Every reason a player sat points to a specific play, or says “no recorded cause” or “end of game”.
  • Each run, 5 random flags are worked out again from the raw box scores and must match, and no flag's average counts its own game.
  • This file: nothing loaded from the internet, no sideways scrolling on a phone, sampled minutes match the database, and every data issue marker shows.
